placement: Before original practice and assessment; original activity phases remain unmodified

R01.teacher: Provide a fresh ramp-height results table with three runs per height. Ask pairs to identify the changed, measured and controlled variables, then compare the repeated measurements.
R01.pupils: Annotate the variables, compare three readings per condition and write a conclusion citing two values; explain why repeat readings matter.

R02.teacher: Provide separate cards showing inhalation, touching a hot object and passing urine. Ask pupils to connect the organ or system to each event and explain its function.
R02.pupils: Trace the air route, match the stimulus to a protective response and identify one waste-removal organ; explain each choice on three labelled cards.

R03.teacher: Distribute animal cards for a fish, frog, bird, mammal and reptile, with breathing clues. Ask pupils to distinguish backbone classification from breathing organs.
R03.pupils: Sort the animals into vertebrate groups, match the breathing clues and justify two matches using the cards.

R04.teacher: Provide new pictures of roots growing towards water and a plant in light. Ask pupils to distinguish responses to stimuli from the requirements for photosynthesis.
R04.pupils: Complete a stimulus-response chart, then label water, carbon dioxide, sunlight, sugar and oxygen on the photosynthesis diagram and explain the distinction.

R05.teacher: Set up a torch and opaque object; provide a mirror and a diagram of a straw in water. Guide pupils to compare one changed position and observe the other two effects.
R05.pupils: Sketch two shadows with the changed position labelled; draw the reflected light path and explain the apparent bend of the straw using the word refraction.

R06.teacher: Give pupils two room diagrams with hard and soft surfaces. Use a simple clap demonstration at a safe sound level and ask them to compare sound reflection.
R06.pupils: Draw the outgoing and reflected sound paths, compare the room surfaces and propose a noise-reduction measure supported by an explanation.

R07.teacher: Supply cards for sunlight, wind, coal and natural gas alongside a fan and a torch diagram. Ask pupils to distinguish energy sources from energy forms.
R07.pupils: Sort the sources as renewable or non-renewable, draw labelled energy transformation arrows for the fan and torch, and identify the useful output.

R08.teacher: Provide a property-results chart for wood, metal and plastic. Assign the design of a handle and a transparent cover; ask pupils to compare evidence rather than guess.
R08.pupils: Recommend a suitable material for each purpose, cite two relevant observations from the chart and explain why one alternative is less suitable.

R09.teacher: Use a globe and lamp to model Earth rotating; show a picture of a supported ball and a falling ball. Ask pupils to distinguish the two explanations.
R09.pupils: Mark day and night on the globe, demonstrate rotation, and add gravity arrows to both ball diagrams with a short explanation of why the supported ball stays in place.

R10.teacher: Use a ruler, safe light load and fulcrum to compare two lever arrangements. Provide a picture of a familiar tool containing simple machines.
R10.pupils: Predict and compare effort when the load distance changes, record the comparison, and label two simple-machine mechanisms on the tool.

R01.teacher: Give pairs a fresh paper-plane results chart with several trials per condition. Ask them to identify the variables and check whether the conclusion follows from the measured distances.
R01.pupils: Annotate the changed, measured and controlled variables; compare the trial results and write a conclusion using two values with a fair-test justification.

R02.teacher: Provide a joint-protection diagram and blank heart–lungs–heart pathway. Ask pupils to trace the movement of blood and explain how the respiratory and circulatory systems cooperate.
R02.pupils: Label a joint and a protective bone, complete the blood-flow arrows and explain how oxygen from the lungs reaches other body parts.

R03.teacher: Give a new food web with a producer, insect, bird and predator. Provide animal-defence clue cards; ask pupils to connect each defence to the relevant threat.
R03.pupils: Annotate the food web, predict a consequence of reducing the insect population, and justify one defence by naming the threat it reduces.

R04.teacher: Provide cards showing thick stems, waxy surfaces, floating fruits and hooked fruits. Ask pupils to distinguish habitat adaptations from seed dispersal mechanisms.
R04.pupils: Match each feature to its benefit or dispersal route and explain two predictions using the visible feature as evidence.

R05.teacher: Using only low-voltage classroom circuit equipment or diagrams, present two parallel branches and a switch. Give a separate picture of a damaged electrical plug.
R05.pupils: Trace complete and open paths, predict which lamp lights in each switch position, then state a safe action for the damaged plug without touching it.

L39.teacher: Provide two safe-temperature water samples, thermometers and a recording table. Demonstrate the correct probe position and ask pupils to repeat the reading independently.
L39.pupils: Measure and record each sample in degrees Celsius, compare the readings and explain that temperature measures how hot or cold an object is, while heat is energy transferred due to a temperature difference.

R06.teacher: Provide three thermometer illustrations and drawings of two bridge joints. Ask pupils to read the scales and relate the joint gaps to expansion.
R06.pupils: Record three temperatures with units, compare the readings and annotate a bridge joint to explain how its gap accommodates expansion.

R07.teacher: Provide results from iron nails kept in dry air, damp air and water with limited air. Show pictures of painted and scratched gates.
R07.pupils: Compare the observations to identify the conditions for rusting, then explain how a coating protects iron and why a scratched area needs repair.

R08.teacher: Provide a diagram of water evaporating from a surface, forming droplets and falling as rain. Ask pupils to organise the process cards and explain each transition.
R08.pupils: Arrange the cards in sequence, label evaporation and condensation using state-change arrows and explain how droplets can form rain.

L56.teacher: Provide four labelled-source constellation outline cards and shuffled matching cards for Orion, Big Dipper, Southern Cross and Scorpion. Discuss one documented direction or seasonal use without assuming year-round visibility.
L56.pupils: Match and sketch the four patterns, identify two from unlabelled outlines and explain one use of a named constellation, noting that visibility depends on place and time.

R09.teacher: Provide eight Moon observation cards and two constellation diagrams. Ask pupils to arrange the four main phases first, then distinguish the two star patterns.
R09.pupils: Sequence the four phases, explain the order using observed shapes, identify the constellation patterns and state one use of the Southern Cross.

R10.teacher: Provide labelled and unlabelled drawings of scissors and another familiar tool combining simple machines. Ask pupils to compare the movement of handles and cutting edges.
R10.pupils: Label the pivot, lever and wedge on scissors, explain each function and compare with the other tool using its labelled mechanisms.
